articles.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
articles.summary:
The GoAhead embedded web server loaded a certificate revocation list into its default TLS backend but never turned revocation checking on, so a revoked client certificate could still pass login on affected setups.

The flaw is in builds that use the OpenSSL backend with mutual-TLS, where the server checks a client certificate and vice versa, and a revocation list is configured to block revoked

articles.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
articles.summary:
Apple on Monday backported fixes for a high-severity security flaw that was exploited in real-world cyber attacks to older devices.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS score: 8.8), is an out-of-bounds write affecting CoreGraphics that could result in arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted file.

articles.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
articles.summary:
Microsoft has fixed a flaw in its Authenticator app for Android that let a malicious app with no permissions pose as a trusted Microsoft app, such as Teams, and collect sign-in tokens for a victim's work account.

Microsoft tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-80097 and fixed it in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246, so anyone using the app should update.

articles.title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
articles.summary:
An attacker who gained access to Keystone's website obtained the key that its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, the company said in a statement on October 26.

articles.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
articles.summary:
Fake login pages are nothing new, but generative AI is making them easier to build and more convincing. Attackers can recreate familiar login screens, impersonate trusted brands and tailor phishing attempts to specific employees or organizations.

articles.summary:

articles.title: Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers
articles.summary:
A criminal using the Amadey malware can no longer access or steal data from 180,000 infected computers around the world, including some in Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) says. The agency's operators gained access to the criminal's operation's backend and cut it off from those computers.

articles.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
articles.summary:
OpenAI's compaction feature, which shrinks a long conversation to save space, could be turned into a way to copy a model's hidden reasoning out in plain text, security firm Xint has shown.

articles.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
articles.summary:
The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has issued an alert warning of unauthorized remote access to video surveillance systems manufactured by Dahua.
